exposure: Race/ethnicity (Filipino, Native Hawaiian, other Pacific Islander, Japanese, Chinese, white)
outcome: Vaginal birth after Cesarean (VBAC) delivery rates
cohort: 75,725 childbirth hospitalizations in Hawaii from 2008 to 2012
finding: Significant variation in maternal quality and safety outcomes was observed among Asian and Pacific Islander subgroups, with Native Hawaiians experiencing better outcomes than whites and Chinese and Japanese women having higher rates of obstetric trauma.
mod_finding: Chinese and Japanese women had significantly higher rates of obstetric trauma during vaginal deliveries, Filipinos and Other Pacific Islanders had higher rates of Cesarean deliveries, Native Hawaiians had lower rates of obstetric trauma during vaginal deliveries, Other Pacific Islanders had higher rates of VBACs, and Japanese women had lower rates of uncomplicated VBACs.
